newsitem.title: USA: MetLife gets OK to write property insurance in N.J.
newsitem.headline: MetLife gets OK to write property insurance in N.J.

text.p: Metropolitan Life Insurance Co won permission from New Jersey regulators for its property and casualty affiliate to write automobile, homeowners and related insurance in the state.

"This is the first time in recent memory that a major national insurance company has sought approval to enter the New Jersey insurance market," New Jersey Insurance Commissioner Elizabeth Randall said.
"We will have more choices in a more competitive market and that is good for consumers," she said in a statement.
Metropolitan Property and Casualty Insurance Co is known for its group marketing approach to auto and homeowners insurance sales.

Under the group marketing approach, Met Property and Casualty will set up payroll deduction programs with New Jersey employers, making it easy and convenient for employees to purchase the coverage they need, the New Jersey insurance department said.
Those policies will be offered at a discount because the company will pass on the savings of writing insurance through such a distribution system, the department said.
